required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh (M, N) output of X's dtype inside run().

One kernel pass over all M*N elements: derive the block coordinates (i // T, j // T) of each element, fetch the scale from S (per-element gather or per-tile hoisted load), multiply X by it, masked store. No expanded scale map in global memory.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The expanded (M, N) scale map is materialised with PyTorch, reproducing the reference on the host.
Host-side index construction for the scale map (reference-style).
The multiply is performed by PyTorch on the host instead of the kernel.
Writing into or returning an input violates the fresh-output / no-mutation rules.
Scale indexing must use floor division of the row and column by the block side.

required_evidence.message: No kernel-level store found; the multiply must be done by a kernel.
No floor-division block-index evidence for the scale lookup.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (M, N) tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() with X's dtype and must not share storage with X or S

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: the output allocation, any flat/2-D views and the single elementwise kernel. No cached state, no copy or cast of X or S, no materialised expanded scale map, no second pass.
